title: Fire safety scenarios sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 11 (Fire safety scenarios sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 11: The fire triangle and fire safety. To understand how the fire triangle explains how fires start and how they are put out

questions.q: A fire blanket is put over a pan fire. Which side of the triangle is removed?
questions.model: What does the blanket do? Covers the fire. What can no longer reach the flame? Air, so oxygen. So the oxygen side is removed and the fire goes out.

questions.q: Why must you not use water on an electrical fire?
questions.a: Water conducts electricity, so you could be electrocuted.

questions.q: Core: For five fires (bin, pan of oil, TV, forest, gas cooker), say the best way to put it out and which side is removed.
questions.a: Bin: water (heat); pan of oil: fire blanket, turn off heat (oxygen, heat); TV: power off, CO₂ extinguisher (oxygen); forest: firebreak (fuel); gas cooker: turn off gas (fuel).
questions.model: Teacher does the bin first: paper fire, use water, removes heat.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why a chip-pan fire becomes a fireball when water is added. Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Water sinks below the hot oil, boils instantly to steam, which expands and throws burning oil droplets into the air.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain the rule 'get out, stay out, call 999' using what smoke contains.
questions.a: Smoke contains carbon monoxide and hot toxic gases that can kill in minutes, so escape is safer than fighting the fire.

questions.q: Which is NOT a side of the fire triangle?
Big question: how does a fire blanket put out a pan fire?
questions.a: It cuts off the oxygen supply, removing one side of the fire triangle.
